preferred: conception / grasp of an individual meaning
why: It supplies the individual conceptual content prior to propositionally assessable assent.
source: al-Mustaṣfā, OpenITI V01P009–010; Miʿyār and Miḥakk cited in V01P009

preferred: assent to a proposition / assertoric assent
why: Negation or affirmation between two conceived terms creates the truth-apt proposition.
It explains the linguistic expression by a known synonym rather than defining the thing.
Distinguishes its object by a set of attributes without recovering all essential constituents.
States constitutive essentials of the quiddity; distinct from the fact that the thing exists.
The answer to mā huwa, asking what the thing is essentially.
Constitutive of what the thing is, not merely inseparable from it.
Can accompany a thing necessarily while remaining conceptually subsequent to its quiddity.
May depart, or can be conceived as absent, without loss of quiddity. Not every occurrence equals Aristotelian accidental substance.
Relative places in the Porphyrian ordering described in the text.

preferred: demonstration; conclusive proof when epistemically warranted
why: A formally valid inference does not yield certainty unless the premises are certain; compare Opwis’s analysis of Ghazālī’s qiyās.
source: al-Mustaṣfā, OpenITI V01P009–010; Opwis, “Syllogistic Logic in Islamic Legal Theory”

preferred: explanatory cause (logic); operative ground (legal analogy), by context
why: The same term serves different functions in the first support on definition and in legal analysis.
source: al-Mustaṣfā, V01P011 vs V01P007; Hallaq and Opwis
